get.description: Liveness + database check, used by Docker Compose and Caddy.

post.description: Send a 6-digit login code by SMS (locally: written to the server console).
Check the code and start a session (about 60 days). The account is created on first login.

get.description: Who is logged in. Also sets the CSRF cookie, so the app calls it first, before the login form.

post.description: Register a company; the logged-in person becomes its owner. A wrong code creates nothing.

get.description: Pending invitations for the logged-in phone number, from any company.

post.description: Join the location. Works only for the invited phone number; anyone else gets 404.

get.description: All invitations of a location, newest first (the manager sees who has not answered yet).

post.description: Invite a person by phone number. No SMS is sent; they see the invitation after logging in.

get.description: The manager's start screen: every location they run, the state of its current period and who is missing.

post.description: A new location starts with the good-practice rules switched on (or follows its group's rules).

patch.description:
Name, address, group, period length, default deadline, handing over given-away shifts without approval;
archiving (owner only) instead of deleting.

delete.description:
Delete a location added by mistake (owner only): one without employees and without any schedule period.
A location that has worked is archived instead, so its schedules and hours stay.

Delete a location group (owner only). Its locations stay, without a group, and keep working as before:
each one gets the group's rules and weights it was using as its own.

post.description: Enter a free-access code. Extends access from its current end date; works also after it has expired.

patch.description: Move the availability deadline (the day the manager will arrange the schedule).

delete.description:
Delete a period added by mistake (e.g. wrong dates), with its drafts. A period whose schedule was ever
published stays: employees saw it and hours are counted from it.

post.description:
"Poproś o dyspozycje": an in-app notice with the period and the deadline for every active employee of the
location (or only those who have not finished). Nothing is arranged automatically: the manager arranges the
schedule when the deadline has passed or everyone has answered.
Start arranging schedules, one run per location. Answers at once; poll `GET /generation-runs/{id}`.
Stop arranging: nothing is saved, the earlier draft stays, and the generation is not counted.

get.description: My published shifts from today on, who works with me, and my hours per month. Works in read-only mode.
One version of a location's schedule: the grid, the three scores, rules, unmet requests and history.

Why this shift has its person (or nobody), and what each person with the position would change.
Quick checks with the validator, no solver; the same list is the manual editor's choice of people.

post.description:
Validate a manual change before saving it (e.g. while dragging): new problems, the new scores and the other
shifts of the person at the same time (the screen asks whether to take the person off them).

get.description:
What dropping this shift's person on each other shift would do (swap or move): new problems and scores.
Asked once when a drag starts, so the answer for every shift is there before the manager hovers over it.

patch.description:
Save a manual change (one shift, or two for a swap), also on days that have passed. A change that breaks
a hard rule is refused with the reasons, unless `force` is set: the manager has the last word. With
`remove_clashes` the person is first taken off their other shifts at the same time.

get.description:
Where one person could work in this schedule, for colouring the grid while the manager moves them: every
shift of their positions that they do not hold, with their calendar mark. Calendar and overlaps only (fast);
the rules are checked when the manager picks a shift. `moving_shift_id`: the shift the person is being
dragged away from, so it does not count as "another shift at that time".

post.description: Pin (or unpin) the person on a shift: arranging the schedule again keeps pinned people in place.

One more person needed on a shift that day: an empty place in the draft, kept when arranging again
(the date's staffing in the location's settings gets the same number).

delete.description:
One person fewer needed on a shift that day: the place leaves the draft (with whoever had it) and the
date's staffing gets the same number.

post.description: Correct a published schedule: a new draft copy (or the newest draft, if there already is one).
Publish the newest draft: employees see it in "Mój grafik"; the previous version stays as history.

get.description: My availability for a period; without `period_id`, the nearest period that is collecting availability.

put.description: Save the marked days (saved at once after every tap or drag; "Cofnij" sends the previous states).

get.description: My availability between two dates (a month on the screen). Open all the time: no period is needed.

put.description: Save marked days, with or without a request from the manager (saved at once after every tap or drag).

post.description: "Powtarzaj co tydzień do [data]": the chosen weekdays get this state from the period start until that date.
"Skopiuj z poprzedniego miesiąca": each day takes the state of the same weekday 4-5 weeks earlier.
"Gotowe": tells the manager I have finished. Days left unmarked mean "mogę".

get.description: My requests for a period, or (without `period_id`) the ones I wrote for a month with no period yet.

post.description: "Coś jeszcze?": a request in words for things the calendar cannot say. Only managers read it.

patch.description:
Correct how my request was understood: write it again, or say "that is not what I meant" (then the
manager reads it as written). The same hands a request the assistant refused over to the manager.

delete.description: Take back my own request while the period is still collecting availability.

get.description: Employees × days of the period: what each person marked, who finished, what changed after the deadline.
Requests in words for this period, oldest first. Only managers see them.

patch.description: The manager rejects a request, or marks it as more or less important than usual.

post.description: Hand a request to the assistant again: one that came while it was switched off, or when the call failed.

get.description: Everything the location settings screen shows.

delete.description:
Also removes its staffing and takes it from people. A position that a saved schedule uses is kept hidden
(old schedules still show its name), so the manager can always get rid of it.

patch.description: New hours apply to schedules arranged from now on; saved schedules keep the hours they had.

delete.description: Removes its staffing too. Saved schedules keep their shifts (with the hours copied).

put.description:
The whole weekly table at once: how many people of each position every shift needs on each weekday.
Cells with 0 (or left out) mean nobody.

Staffing of one date (e.g. Christmas Eve), set from the calendar. It replaces the weekday's staffing for the
shifts and positions that differ; everything left out, or equal to the usual, follows the weekday again.

post.description: A day the location is closed: the generator schedules nobody there that day.

get.description:
People who work in this location (as their main location or an extra one): active first, then switched
off; by surname.

post.description:
A manager who also works shifts adds themselves to the schedule of a location they manage, with every
position of the location (they can stand in for anyone; positions can be narrowed afterwards).

patch.description:
Name, positions, experience level, monthly maximum and target, or switching the person off
(history stays).

delete.description:
Remove the person from a location (`location_id`, by default their main one). From their only location
it is for good: shifts in saved schedules and their hours stay; a plain employee loses access to the company
and can come back only through a new invitation. From one of several locations only that location goes; the
person keeps working in the others (docs/plan.md, section 27).

put.description:
Save the whole list. In a location, a rule set exactly like in the group (also its place) keeps following
the group; anything else becomes the location's own setting.

post.description:
What the change would mean on the last schedule of each location, checked without arranging it again
(the generator runs only in the background).

get.description: Hours of published shifts in a month, per person and location (the locations this manager runs).
The same report as a CSV file (semicolons and decimal commas, so a Polish spreadsheet opens it as is).

post.description:
'Oddaj zmianę': everyone who could take my shift gets an in-app notification. It stays mine until the
manager approves someone.
The giver keeps the shift after all.

get.description: 'Zmiany do wzięcia': shifts given away in the company that I can take now (or already said 'Biorę' to).

post.description:
'Biorę': the managers of the location decide; the shift is not mine until they approve. With the location's
rule "bez zatwierdzania" it is mine at once (status "approved").

get.description: 'Oddane zmiany' in my locations: open ones, those waiting for my decision, and the last two weeks.

post.description: The volunteer gets the shift in the published schedule (checked by the validator again).

get.description: Published shifts of the location (two weeks back, two months ahead) for "Zmień obsadę".
Who the manager can put on this published shift: people who can come first, then those with problems.

post.description: The manager puts another person on a published shift, without anyone's "Weź zmianę".
What the validator says about two people exchanging their published shifts (nothing is saved).
Two people exchange their published shifts; both are told in the app.
The manager looks for someone to take an employee's shift: the same offer as the employee's "Oddaj zmianę".
The manager ends an offer: the shift stays with the person who gave it away.

get.description: My newest notifications, newest first, and how many I have not seen. Works in read-only mode.

delete.description: Remove all of my notifications in this company.

post.description: Mark my notifications as seen (not company data, so allowed in read-only mode too).

delete.description: Remove one of my notifications for good (the "X" on it). Allowed in read-only mode, like marking as seen.

get.description: The current manager's latest 50 messages in this location, oldest first.

post.description: Tell the assistant in words what to change in how this location's schedule is arranged.

get.description: Poll this until the status is no longer "queued".

post.description: Accept the plan: the rule list and the instructions change as the plan's lines say.
Throw the plan away; nothing changes.

get.description: The manager's instructions about people, most important first.

delete.description: Undo one rule agreed in the chat: the period uses the location's own setting for it again.

get.description: What the manager may copy from the previous period into this one. Nothing is copied by itself.

post.description: Copy the ticked agreements of the previous period into this one (or into the waiting list).

put.description: Change the order (importance) of the instructions; the list must name each of them once.

ErrorOut.description: Every error response: a plain-language Polish message that can be shown to the person as is.
ErrorOut.title: ErrorOut

in_draft.description: An unpublished draft still has people on this day; arrange again to clear it.
in_draft.title: In Draft

in_published.description: The published schedule still has people on this day.
in_published.title: In Published

DayStaffingIn.description: What one date needs. A shift and position left out goes back to the weekday's usual staffing.
DayStaffingIn.title: DayStaffingIn
